lesson.title: Boot Verbs: e→ie, o→ue & e→i Under Stress
lesson.subtitle: Why querer (quiero/queremos), poder (puedo/podemos), tener (tienes/tenemos), and pedir (pido/pedimos) split their stem vowel only when stressed

hook.title: Not 'Irregular' — Just Stress-Driven!
hook.content: Textbooks terrify learners with long lists of 'stem-changing boot verbs'. Language Transfer reveals the simple acoustic truth: in Vulgar Latin, stressed short E and short O stretched out into two-vowel diphthongs (e → ie, o → ue). Whenever your voice stresses the stem (yo, tú, él/ella/usted, ellos), the vowel splits: quiero, puedes, duermo ('I sleep'), empiezo ('I start'), prefiero ('I prefer'). Whenever the stress steps onto the nosotros ending (-emos / -imos / -amos), the stem vowel stays single: queremos, podemos, dormimos, empezamos, preferimos!

footnotes.title: Why Teachers Call Them 'Boot Verbs'
footnotes.content: If you draw a box around the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd person singular on the left and 3rd person plural at the bottom right — leaving out nosotros in the top right — the outline looks just like a boot!

pattern.title: The Three Vowel Shifts: e→ie, o→ue, and e→i
pattern.content:
1) e → ie: querer (quiero / queremos), empezar (empiezo / empezamos), preferir (prefiero / preferimos).
2) o → ue: poder ('to be able to / can' → puedo, puedes, puede / podemos), dormir ('to sleep' → duermo / dormimos).
3) e → i (in -ir verbs like pedir 'to ask for / order'): pido, pides, pide / pedimos!
pattern.trap_note: Never put *por after pedir when asking for an item (*pedir por un café). Pedir already contains 'for': Quiero pedir un café!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: I can / am able to (poder: o→ue)

exercises.target_answer: puedo, puedes, podemos, prefiero, pido, dormir
exercises.meaning: I can / am able to (poder: o→ue), you can (poder: o→ue), we can (unstressed stem!), I prefer (preferir: e→ie), I order / ask for (pedir: e→i), to sleep (duermo / dormimos)
exercises.explanation: When the stem is stressed, the vowel splits (puedo, prefiero, pido); when -emos/-imos takes the stress, the stem stays unchanged (podemos, preferimos, pedimos).

exercises.prompt: Spanish dormir ('to sleep', duermo 'I sleep') shares its Latin root with which English word for a university sleeping hall?
exercises.meaning: a dormitory is literally 'a place for sleeping'
exercises.explanation: Latin dormīre gave Spanish dormir and English dormitory and dormant.

exercises.prompt: Complete the Boot-Verb Stress Matrix by writing the 'yo' (stressed stem) form of 'poder' ('I can'):
exercises.row_law: Each row shows one of the three Spanish boot-verb vowel shifts (e→ie, o→ue, e→i).
exercises.column_law: Column 1 stresses the stem vowel (splitting it); Column 2 stresses -emos/-imos (keeping the stem vowel single).
exercises.explanation: In yo puedo, the stress lands on the stem, splitting o into ue; in nosotros podemos, the stress moves onto -emos!
¿Puedes ('Can you') + confirmar ('confirm', bare infinitive) + la reservación?

exercises.idea: say that you want to order a coffee (using pedir)
cues: to order / ask for (needs no 'for'!) → pedir
exercises.meaning: I want to order a coffee
exercises.explanation: Quiero pedir un café — pedir already means 'to ask FOR / to order', so never add *por after pedir!

diagnosis.cue: pedir means 'to ask for / order' all by itself: pedir un café.

summary.outcome: Conjugate e→ie (querer, empezar, preferir), o→ue (poder, dormir), and e→i (pedir) boot verbs by following vocal stress.

use_example.german: Puedo ir hoy, pero prefiero ir mañana.
use_example.english: I can go today, but I prefer to go tomorrow.

summary.takeaway: Stressed stem = split vowel (quiero, puedo, pido); stressed nosotros ending = single vowel (queremos, podemos, pedimos).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([11] Adjective Agreement): build full noun phrases with gender and plural concord.

twist.explanation: No puedo ir hoy chains no puedo + bare infinitive ir.

querer.etymology_derivation: Latin quaerere ('to seek, ask for') evolved in Spanish to 'to want' and 'to love'. When you make an inquiry in English, you are asking what you want.

poder.english_meaning: to be able to, can (puedo: I can)
poder.shift_rule: Boot verb o → ue (puedo, puedes, puede, podemos)
poder.etymology_derivation: Vulgar Latin *potēre — root of potent and potential.

puedo.english_meaning: I can, I am able to
puedo.etymology_derivation: o splits into ue under stress.

puedes.etymology_derivation: Chains directly with a bare infinitive.

dormir.etymology_derivation: Latin dormīre — English dormitory and dormant.

empezar.english_meaning: to begin, to start (empiezo: I start)
empezar.shift_rule: Boot verb e → ie (takes a before infinitive)
empezar.context_phrase: La clase empieza a las nueve.
empezar.etymology_derivation: Takes a before a following infinitive: empiezo a comprender ('I'm starting to understand').

pedir.english_meaning: to ask for, to order (pido: I order/ask for)
pedir.shift_rule: Boot verb e → i (pido, pides, pide, pedimos)
pedir.context_translation: I want to order a coffee.
pedir.etymology_derivation: Latin petere ('to seek/ask for') — English petition and appetite. Needs no 'for'!

preferir.etymology_derivation: Stem-changing e → ie in the boot: prefiero, prefieres, prefiere.

tener.etymology_derivation: Latin tenēre ('to hold'). While other tongues used 'have' (like French avoir), Spanish promoted 'hold' (tener) to main possession.

tenemos.shift_rule: 1st person plural of tener (outside the boot!)
tenemos.etymology_derivation: Because the stress moves onto the ending (-ne-mos), the stem vowel e stays unchanged!
